下面按论文 **Results 章节原本标题/子标题** 来梳理。整体故事其实很清楚：**先证明模型预测性能很高，但这不等于模型真的用了医学上正确的通路；然后用 matched-control perturbation audit 逐步证明：有些通路是真支持，有些只是 target-only 扰动造成的假阳性，有些高度依赖扰动算子或模型架构。** fileciteturn1file1

---

# IV. RESULTS

## A. Classification Context: The Limits of Discrimination Metrics  
## 分类性能背景：判别指标的局限

这一节的作用是**先把传统性能交代清楚，但马上指出传统性能不够**。

论文先展示：ResNet 在五个疾病上 AUROC 都超过 0.98，Micro-F1 为 0.736；SE-ResNet 和 ResNet 几乎没有差别；Transformer 在 BBB 上表现还可以，但在 SBRAD、AFIB 等节律类疾病上明显弱；XGBoost Clinical-MVP 特征模型比简单特征模型更好，但仍低于 raw-signal 深度模型。fileciteturn1file4

这一节的核心不是炫性能，而是铺垫一个关键矛盾：

> 这些疾病从 AUROC 看都“解决了”，但 AUROC 只能说明模型能区分阳性/阴性，不能说明模型是否真的使用了临床上对应的信号区域。

也就是说，模型可能诊断 1AVB 很准，但它未必真的主要看 PR interval；模型可能诊断 AFIB 很准，但未必主要看 RR irregularity 或 atrial activity。  
所以这一节提出 Results 的主线：**从 discrimination performance 转向 pathway-specific evidence。**

---

## B. The Case for Matched Controls: 1AVB as Anchor Demonstration  
## 为什么必须有 matched controls：以 1AVB 作为核心示范

这一大节是 Results 的核心叙事起点。它用 1AVB 说明：**只看 target perturbation 会得出错误结论，必须比较 matched controls。**

---

### 1) Why Target-Only Perturbation Is Insufficient: The 1AVB Reversal  
### 为什么只做目标区域扰动不够：1AVB 反转案例

这里讲的是全文最重要的负例。

1AVB 的临床预期通路是 **PR prolongation / AV conduction timing**。如果模型真的依赖 PR 信息，那么扰动 PR-window 应该显著降低 1AVB 识别能力。

结果确实看起来支持这个说法：PR-window occlusion 让 AUROC 从 0.9853 降到 0.7597，ΔAUROC 约为 -0.226；在 1AVB 阳性样本上，PR-window 扰动使 false-negative probability 增加约 32.7%。如果按普通 perturbation explainability 论文的写法，到这里就可以声称：“模型使用了 PR-segment 信息。”fileciteturn1file0

但 matched QRS control 改变了结论：  
QRS occlusion 的破坏更大，ΔAUROC 约为 -0.351，比 PR-window 还严重。于是 ResNet 的 ASS 变成负值，ASS = -0.332；SE-ResNet 也为负。fileciteturn1file0

这就形成了论文的核心反转：

> PR 扰动确实有用，但它不是最特异的；模型对 QRS control 更敏感。因此这是 PR sensitivity，不是 PR specificity。

这一节要讲清楚的是：**target-only perturbation 只能证明某区域“有影响”，不能证明该区域“比相邻控制区域更关键”。**  
所以 1AVB 被分类为 **Not supported**，不是因为 PR 没用，而是因为 PR 没有超过 matched control。

---

### 2) External Validation Confirms PR Sensitivity but Not PR Specificity  
### 外部验证确认：PR 敏感性存在，但 PR 特异性不存在

这一小节把 1AVB 反转从 CODE-15% 推到 PTB-XL 外部数据集。

在 PTB-XL fold 10 上，PR-window perturbation 仍然造成明显 AUROC 下降，说明模型在外部数据上也确实对 PR-region 信息敏感。  
但 QRS-window perturbation 造成更大下降，因此 PTB-XL 上 ASS 仍然为负。论文给出 ResNet external ASS 约为 -0.251 / 表 X 中为 -0.278；SE-ResNet、Transformer 也没有形成正向支持。fileciteturn1file0

这里的逻辑是：

> 如果 1AVB 只是在内部数据失败，可能是 CODE label 或数据偏差问题；但外部 cardiologist-validated PTB-XL 也复现了 “PR sensitivity without PR specificity”，说明这个 matched-control failure 很稳。

所以 1AVB 成为全文最强的 methodological warning：**一个看似符合医学常识的 target perturbation 结果，在 matched-control 框架下可能完全站不住。**

---

### 3) QRS Occlusion (BBB) and RR Regularization (AFIB)  
### QRS 扰动用于 BBB，RR regularization 用于 AFIB

这一节开始把 audit 从 1AVB 推广到其他疾病通路。

对 BBB，尤其 CRBBB 和 CLBBB，临床预期通路是 **QRS morphology**。QRS occlusion 会显著降低 BBB 检测能力：CRBBB 和 CLBBB 的 AUROC 都出现较大下降。这说明 BBB 相关模型确实对 QRS 信息敏感。更重要的是，后续在 primary linear interpolation operator 下，QRS target 相比 ST/random controls 仍然占优，因此 BBB 会成为后面最稳定的 positive result。

对 AFIB，论文先测试 RR irregularity。方法是把每个 heartbeat time-warp 到 median RR interval，从而破坏 RR irregularity，同时尽量保留 QRS morphology。结果 RR regularization 对 AFIB AUROC 的影响很小，ΔAUROC 约 -0.007，而且 beat-permutation control 几乎一样。fileciteturn1file0

这一节的结论是：

> BBB 的 QRS morphology pathway 有强阳性迹象；但 AFIB 的 RR irregularity pathway 在 ResNet 中没有形成 pathway-specific evidence。

这为后面 “AFIB 不支持” 和 “BBB 支持” 做铺垫。

---

### 4) AFIB Atrial-Window Audit  
### AFIB atrial-window 审计

因为 RR irregularity 没有给出支持，论文进一步测试 AFIB 的另一个可能机制：**atrial activity / P-wave absence**。

这一步很关键，因为 AFIB 理论上既可能依赖 RR irregularity，也可能依赖 P-wave absence / atrial activity。作者用 primary linear interpolation operator 对 atrial window 做扰动，并和 controls 比较。

结果是：在 primary linear interpolation 下，AFIB atrial-window ASS 在三个 raw-signal 架构、两个数据集上全部为负。CODE 上 ResNet -0.200、SE-ResNet -0.229、Transformer -0.402；PTB-XL 上 ResNet -0.126、SE-ResNet -0.073、Transformer -0.387。fileciteturn1file0

这说明：

> AFIB 的 atrial-window target perturbation 没有超过 matched controls，因此不能声称模型使用了 atrial activity pathway。

这里还特别强调 operator artifact：早期 zero-masking 下 AFIB 曾出现正向 ASS，而且跨数据集方向一致；但换成 continuity-preserving 的 linear interpolation 后，这个阳性消失了。因此作者认为 AFIB 的 zero-masking positive 是 hard-boundary artifact。fileciteturn1file0

所以 AFIB 的结论是双重否定：

1. RR irregularity 不支持；  
2. atrial-window 在 primary operator 下也不支持。  

最终 AFIB 被归为 **Not supported**。

---

### 5) Feature-Space Cross-Check for the AFIB Discovery Case [Supplementary]  
### AFIB 的特征空间交叉检查

这一节是补充性的，但对解释 AFIB 很有用。

XGBoost Clinical-MVP 的 feature-group permutation importance 显示：AFIB 检测中，AV Conduction Timing features 的 ΔAUROC 为 0.179，高于 Rhythm & Rate features 的 0.077。fileciteturn1file0

这说明不同模型类别可能依赖不同信息通道：  
raw-signal ResNet/SE-ResNet/Transformer 在 perturbation audit 中没有表现出 RR 或 atrial pathway specificity，但 XGBoost feature-space 反而显示 AFIB 可能依赖某些 AV conduction timing 相关特征。

这一节的作用不是推翻 AFIB 的 Not supported，而是强调：

> audit 应该按模型逐个做，不能把一个模型的解释结论泛化到所有模型。

---

### 6) SBRAD Rate-Pathway Audit  
### SBRAD 低心率通路审计

SBRAD 的临床定义是 sustained low ventricular rate，所以 target perturbation 不是局部窗口遮挡，而是全局 **rate normalization**：把 heartbeat time-warp 到 75 bpm，测试模型是否真的依赖低心率信息。

由于 rate 是全局属性，SBRAD 使用 hybrid protocol：target 是 rate normalization，controls 是 QRS、ST、random non-QRS windows 的 linear interpolation。

结果显示明显的 architecture heterogeneity：

- ResNet：CODE ASS = +0.092，PTB-XL ASS = +0.111，但外部 CI 略微跨 0，所以是 **Evidence-limited**；
- SE-ResNet：CODE 上为负，PTB-XL 上转正，出现 cross-dataset sign reversal，所以是 **Not supported**；
- Transformer：内外部都为负，所以是 **Not supported**。fileciteturn1file3

这一节的故事是：

> SBRAD 的 rate pathway 并不是疾病层面的稳定属性，而是模型架构相关的属性。ResNet 有一定 rate-pathway evidence，但还不够稳；SE-ResNet 和 Transformer 不支持。

---

## C. Model-Level Pathway Evidence Under a Shared Audit Protocol  
## 共享审计协议下的模型级通路证据

这一节把前面分散的疾病案例收束成一个跨架构比较。

作者强调：audit protocol 是 model-agnostic 的，同一套 disease-pathway definition、matched-control region、ASS 计算可以用于 ResNet、SE-ResNet、Transformer。重点不是证明协议能用，而是看 **pathway-specific evidence 是疾病本身的属性，还是模型的属性**。fileciteturn2file0

这一节给出 6 个总结性发现：

### 1. BBB 的 QRS morphology evidence 是 architecture-robust

CRBBB 和 CLBBB 在三个 raw-signal 架构上都表现出正 ASS，且 CI 下界大于 0。外部 PTB-XL 也保持正向。  
因此 CRBBB 和 CLBBB 在 ResNet、SE-ResNet、Transformer 上全部达到 **Pathway-supported**。fileciteturn2file0

这是全文最强 positive result：

> QRS morphology pathway 不仅内部成立，而且跨架构、跨数据集、在 primary operator 下都成立。

---

### 2. AFIB 的 RR-irregularity audit 在三个架构上都是 negative

RR regularization 对 AFIB 的影响接近 0，且不超过 beat-permutation control。  
这说明三个 raw-signal 模型都没有表现出对 RR irregularity 的 primary dependence。

---

### 3. AFIB atrial-window audit 推翻了 zero-masking 阳性

linear interpolation 下，三个架构的 AFIB atrial-window ASS 都为负。  
所以早期 zero-masking 的 AFIB positive 被解释为边界伪影，而不是生理通路证据。fileciteturn2file0

---

### 4. SBRAD 是 model-specific evidence

只有 ResNet 的 SBRAD rate ASS 为正，SE-ResNet 和 Transformer 为负。  
因此 SBRAD 不是 architecture-robust 的通路证据，而是 ResNet-specific 的有限证据。

---

### 5. 1AVB 在所有架构上都是 matched-control failure

PR occlusion 的 PSS 在不同架构上都不小，但 ASS 都不成立：ResNet、SE-ResNet、Transformer 都没有让 PR target 超过 matched QRS control。  
所以 1AVB 的核心结论很稳：**PR sensitivity exists, but PR specificity fails。**

---

### 6. XGBoost feature-space 显示模型类别之间的信息通道不同

XGBoost 的特征消融结果说明，不同模型类可能用不同通路。  
因此这篇论文不把 XGBoost 纳入 waveform matched-control tiering，而是作为 feature-space supporting evidence。

这一节最后的 methodological implication 是：**扰动算子不是实现细节，而是会改变结论的一阶变量。**  
所以 zero-masking 被降级为历史比较，linear interpolation 成为 primary operator。

---

## D. External Transfer as an Audit Stress Test  
## 外部迁移作为审计压力测试

这一节的作用是回答：**这些 pathway 结论能不能跨数据集成立？**

---

### 1) External Feature-Space Support from PTB-XL+  
### 来自 PTB-XL+ 的外部特征空间支持

作者在 PTB-XL+ 的 12SL features 上训练 XGBoost，使用官方 patient-level folds，并在 fold 10 上测试。  
这一节主要说明 feature-level pattern 有一定可迁移性：1AVB 仍然更依赖 timing-rich features，BBB 更依赖 morphology-rich features，SBRAD/AFIB 更偏 rhythm-related features。fileciteturn2file0

但作者也很谨慎：这一节只支持 feature-level transportability，不直接替代 raw-signal frozen transfer audit。

---

### 2) External Audit Credibility Check on PTB-XL  
### PTB-XL 上的外部审计可信度检查

这是外部验证的主结果。

作者把 CODE-trained ResNet 冻结，不 fine-tune，直接迁移到 PTB-XL fold 10。fold 10 是 cardiologist-validated，因此作为主要外部可信度数据集。fileciteturn2file0

结果显示：  
AUROC 在五个疾病上都仍然 > 0.93。CRBBB、CLBBB 几乎不掉；1AVB、SBRAD 有一定下降；AFIB 仍然较好。Threshold retuning 可以提高 F1，但 AUROC 是主要的 threshold-invariant transfer 指标。fileciteturn1file2

更重要的是 pathway audit 的外部结果：

- CRBBB / CLBBB：三个架构外部 ASS 都为正，且 CI > 0，因此 **Pathway-supported**；
- 1AVB：外部仍然为负，因此 **Not supported**；
- AFIB：外部仍然为负，因此 **Not supported**；
- SBRAD-ResNet：外部方向为正，但 CI 跨 0，因此 **Evidence-limited**；
- SBRAD-SE-ResNet：外部为正但内部为负，属于 sign reversal，不能支持；
- SBRAD-Transformer：内外部都不支持。fileciteturn1file3

这一节的核心作用是把 audit 从 “内部解释” 提升到 “跨数据集解释稳定性”。

---

## E. Case-Study Audit Summary  
## 案例研究式审计总结

这一节是 Results 的最终归纳，Table X 是最关键表格。它把五个 disease-pathway pair × 三个 raw-signal architecture 的结果全部分成三类：

- **PS = Pathway-supported**
- **EL = Evidence-limited**
- **NS = Not supported**

总结果是：

> 15 个 model-disease pairs 中，6 个 Pathway-supported，1 个 Evidence-limited，8 个 Not supported。

---

### 1) Audit Score Summary  
### 审计分数总结

Table X 是全文最重要的结果表。核心结果如下：fileciteturn1file3

| Disease-pathway | ResNet | SE-ResNet | Transformer | 结论 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1AVB / PR prolongation | NS | NS | NS | PR 有敏感性，但没有特异性 |
| CRBBB / QRS morphology | PS | PS | PS | 稳定支持 |
| CLBBB / QRS morphology | PS | PS | PS | 稳定支持 |
| SBRAD / low ventricular rate | EL | NS | NS | ResNet 有有限证据，架构依赖强 |
| AFIB / atrial activity | NS | NS | NS | primary operator 下不支持 |

---

### 1AVB — Anchor demonstration of matched-control necessity  
### 1AVB：matched-control 必要性的核心示范

1AVB 是最重要的 negative result。  
PR-window perturbation 很大，但 QRS matched control 更大，因此所有模型都 Not supported。  
它告诉读者：**target perturbation 大，不等于 pathway-specific evidence。**

---

### CRBBB and CLBBB — QRS morphology Pathway-supported on all three architectures  
### CRBBB 和 CLBBB：三个架构均支持 QRS morphology 通路

这是全文最强 positive result。  
CRBBB 和 CLBBB 在 CODE 内部为正，在 PTB-XL 外部也为正，三个架构都支持。  
这说明 QRS morphology pathway 的证据最稳，能跨架构、跨数据集、跨 operator selection 后保持成立。fileciteturn1file3

---

### SBRAD — Architecture-dependent rate-pathway learning  
### SBRAD：架构依赖的低心率通路学习

SBRAD 是中间态。  
ResNet 内部 ASS 为正，外部方向也为正，但外部 CI 跨 0，所以是 Evidence-limited。  
SE-ResNet 和 Transformer 不支持。  
这说明 rate pathway 不是疾病层面的普遍结论，而是模型相关。fileciteturn1file3

---

### AFIB — Operator artifact confirmed on external dataset  
### AFIB：外部数据确认 zero-masking 阳性是算子伪影

AFIB 是 operator-dependence 的典型案例。  
zero-masking 曾给出 positive pattern，但 primary linear interpolation 下，三个架构、两个数据集全为负。  
所以 AFIB 最终是 Not supported。fileciteturn1file0

这部分想表达的是：

> 如果只用 zero-masking，AFIB 会被误判为 Pathway-supported；引入 operator comparison 后，才能发现这是 artifact。

---

## F. Confirmatory Inference: Clustered Bootstrap and Multiplicity Control  
## 确证性推断：患者聚类 bootstrap 与多重比较控制

最后一节是统计稳健性补强。

作者对 15 个外部 primary-operator pathway-specificity tests 做确认性推断，假设是 H0: ASS ≤ 0。  
为了解决同一患者多条 ECG 的相关性，作者使用 patient-level clustered bootstrap；为了解决 15 次检验的多重比较问题，使用 BH-FDR。fileciteturn1file2

结果是：

- 6 个 Pathway-supported pair，也就是 CRBBB 和 CLBBB 在三个架构上的结果，全部通过 FDR；
- SBRAD-ResNet 没有通过 FDR，和 Evidence-limited 的定位一致；
- SBRAD-SE-ResNet 虽然外部显著，但内部为负，存在 sign reversal，所以仍然 Not supported；
- 没有任何 tier assignment 因多重比较控制而改变。fileciteturn1file2

这一节的作用是给最终分层加保险：

> 六个 PS 是统计上稳健的；唯一 EL 的不确定性是真实存在的；NS 不被外部偶然阳性推翻。

---

# 整个 Results 的故事线

可以压缩成一句话：

> 模型分类性能很高，但高 AUROC 不能证明模型用了正确医学通路；matched-control audit 显示，1AVB 的 PR 扰动虽然有效但不特异，AFIB 的 zero-masking 阳性是算子伪影，SBRAD 呈现架构依赖，而 CRBBB/CLBBB 的 QRS morphology 通路在三个架构和外部 PTB-XL 上都稳定成立。

再进一步讲，Results 章节真正想证明的不是“哪个 ECG 病最好识别”，而是：

> **我们提出的 matched-control pathway audit 能区分三类情况：真正的 pathway-specific evidence、有限/不稳定证据、以及 target-only 或 operator artifact 导致的假阳性解释。**

这就是这篇论文 Results 的主线。

## 1. Abstract 已经抓住了正文核心

从正文 Results 来看，核心故事是：

> 高 AUROC 不等于模型使用了医学正确通路；matched-control audit 可以识别 target-only perturbation 的假阳性、operator artifact，以及真正跨数据集稳定的 pathway-specific evidence。

Abstract 里面确实覆盖了这些点：

- **1AVB 作为 anchor case**：PR perturbation 看似有效，但 matched QRS control 反转结论，说明 target-only perturbation 会产生 false-positive pathway claims。
- **operator comparison**：zero-masking 会产生 boundary artifacts，linear interpolation 被设为 primary operator。
- **BBB positive result**：CRBBB/CLBBB 的 QRS morphology pathway 在三个 raw-signal architectures 和外部 PTB-XL 上稳定支持。
- **SBRAD architecture heterogeneity**：ResNet evidence-limited，SE-ResNet 和 Transformer not supported。
- **AFIB negative result**：primary operator 下 AFIB atrial-window ASS 为负，早期 zero-masking positive 是 artifact。
- **最终 tier summary**：15 个 model-disease pairs 中，6 个 Pathway-supported，1 个 Evidence-limited，8 个 Not supported。fileciteturn0file0

所以从“有没有体现正文核心”来说，答案是：**有。**

## 2. 但现在 Abstract 最大问题是“结果堆砌”，不是“主线表达”

现在 Results 段几乎像把 Table X 压缩进了摘要。它很详细，但读起来有点吃力。尤其是这些数字：

> CRBBB ResNet/SE-ResNet/Transformer external ASS: 0.455/0.255/0.427; CLBBB: 0.261/0.330/0.387  
> AFIB ResNet internal/external: -0.200/-0.126; SE-ResNet: -0.229/-0.073; Transformer: -0.402/-0.387

这些数字当然重要，但 Abstract 里列太多，会让读者注意力从“论文贡献”转移到“数值细节”。对于 JBHI 这种期刊，摘要需要精准，但不应该像 Supplementary result summary。

更好的写法应该是：

先讲主发现：

1. 1AVB 证明 target-only perturbation 会误导；
2. BBB 是稳定 pathway-supported；
3. AFIB 暴露 zero-masking artifact；
4. SBRAD 显示 architecture dependence；
5. 总体 tiering 结果。

然后只保留最关键的代表性数字。

---

## 3. Abstract 对“为什么这篇论文重要”的表达还可以更突出

现在 Background 写得不错，但还可以更锋利。

正文真正的新意不是“做了 perturbation”，而是：

> 传统 explanation 方法常常只问“这个区域是否重要”，但本文问的是“这个疾病预期区域是否比 matched anatomical controls 更重要，并且这种结论是否能跨数据集、跨扰动算子成立”。

这个区别非常关键。Abstract 里有写 “sensitivity is not specificity”，这是好句子，但可以更早、更明确地成为主轴。

我建议 Abstract 第一段就突出：

> Existing perturbation explanations often measure sensitivity, but pathway claims require specificity against matched anatomical controls.

这样审稿人一眼就知道你不是又做了一个 saliency/occlusion study，而是在重新定义 explanation evidence 的判据。

---

## 4. Methods 段略显复杂，Evidence-classification rules 可以简化

现在 Methods 段同时讲了：

- model-agnostic matched-control perturbation audit；
- targeted perturbations vs anatomical controls；
- linear interpolation；
- frozen-weight transfer；
- preregistered operator-comparison battery；
- evidence-classification rules；
- five diagnoses；
- four architectures；
- two datasets。

这些都对，但放在 Abstract 里显得很满。

我建议 Methods 段只保留四个核心动作：

> We prespecified disease-relevant target regions and matched anatomical controls, quantified pathway specificity with ASS, evaluated robustness under a predefined continuity-preserving operator and operator-comparison battery, and tested transfer using frozen CODE-trained models on PTB-XL fold 10.

然后把 “per-model evidence-classification rules” 放到最后一句或 Results 里作为 outcome，而不是 Methods 里详细解释。

---

## 5. Results 段最需要重写：从“数字列表”变成“证据层级”

现在 Results 段的问题是：**数字很多，但叙事层级不够。**

建议按证据层级写：

### 第一层：反例 / 方法必要性

1AVB 证明 matched controls 必要。这个必须放最前面，因为它支撑论文方法论。

### 第二层：稳定阳性

CRBBB/CLBBB 是真正 supported 的 pathway evidence。

### 第三层：不稳定/阴性

SBRAD architecture-dependent；AFIB operator artifact；最终 tier summary。

这样读者会觉得 Results 是一个完整故事，而不是五个疾病结果的罗列。

---

## 6. Conclusions 段方向对，但可以更有“take-home message”

现在 Conclusions 说标准 discrimination metrics 不足、matched-control audit 可以区分 pathway-specific signal use 和 artifacts，这个是对的。  
但我觉得还可以更强一点：

> The audit changes the interpretation of high-performing ECG classifiers: some diagnoses are supported by disease-consistent pathways, whereas others remain high-performing but pathway-unsupported.

这句话非常重要，因为它把论文价值讲透了：**不是模型不好，而是高性能模型的证据来源不一定可靠。**

---

# 总体评价

我会这样判断：

| 维度 | 评价 |
|---|---|
| 是否覆盖正文核心 | 是，主要结果基本都写到了 |
| 是否突出方法贡献 | 基本突出，但可以更锋利 |
| 是否清楚表达 Results 故事线 | 部分清楚，但数字堆叠太多 |
| 是否适合 JBHI 审稿人快速理解 | 可以，但还不够顺滑 |
| 最大问题 | Abstract 太像结果表压缩版，缺少层级化叙事 |
| 修改方向 | 减少数字，强化 “sensitivity ≠ specificity → matched-control audit → tiered evidence” 主线 |

我的建议是：**Abstract 不需要大改方向，但需要重写表达结构。**  
正文核心已经在里面了，只是现在没有以最有说服力的顺序呈现。

Beyond Discrimination: A Matched-Control
Pathway Audit for Evaluating Pathway-Specific
Evidence in ECG Classifiers
Anonymous
Abstract—Background: ECG classifiers routinely achieve high
discrimination, yet may rely on clinically irrelevant signal regions.
Existing explanation methods rarely test whether disease-specific
regions dominate over matched anatomical controls, whether
pathway conclusions survive dataset shift, or whether results
are robust to the perturbation operator itself—sensitivity is not
specificity.
Methods: We propose a model-agnostic matched-control per￾turbation audit for evaluating pathway-specific evidence in ECG
classifiers—distinguishing disease-consistent signal use from cor￾related but non-specific features. The protocol compares targeted
perturbations against anatomically adjacent controls, adopts lin￾ear interpolation as a continuity-preserving perturbation to avoid
hard-boundary artifacts, and evaluates pathway specificity under
frozen-weight transfer to an independent cardiologist-validated
dataset. A preregistered operator-comparison battery character￾izes how operator choice affects conclusions. Per-model evidence￾classification rules—pathway-supported, evidence-limited, not
supported—standardize interpretation under operator depen￾dence and external transfer, assigning a tier to each (architecture,
disease) pair rather than aggregating across architectures. Five
diagnoses spanning timing, morphology, and rhythm pathways
serve as a case-study panel across four architectures and two
datasets.
Results: 1AVB is the anchor demonstration: although PR￾segment perturbation produces a large AUROC drop, matched
QRS controls reverse the interpretation, yielding negative
anatomical specificity under the primary linear-interpolation
operator (ResNet ASS= −0.332) and on the external dataset
(ASS= −0.278). This indicates that target-only perturbation can
produce false-positive pathway claims. A preregistered operator￾comparison battery shows that zero-masking creates boundary
artifacts that inflate control-region disruption; linear interpola￾tion is adopted as the primary operator. Under this protocol,
QRS-morphology pathways (CRBBB, CLBBB) reach Pathway￾supported on all three raw-signal architectures: internal positive
ASS with CI> 0 is replicated under frozen-weight transfer to
PTB-XL fold 10 under the same primary operator (CRBBB
ResNet/SE-ResNet/Transformer external ASS: 0.455/0.255/0.427;
CLBBB: 0.261/0.330/0.387). SBRAD reveals architecture het￾erogeneity: ResNet is Evidence-limited (rate pathway positive
internally and externally, ASS 0.092/0.111, but external CI
narrowly crosses zero), while SE-ResNet and Transformer are
Not supported (−0.033/−0.096). AFIB atrial-window ASS is
negative on all architectures under the primary operator on
both datasets (ResNet internal/external: −0.200/−0.126; SE￾ResNet: −0.229/−0.073; Transformer: −0.402/−0.387), reveal￾ing the initial zero-masking positive as operator artifact. Over￾all, 6 of 15 model-disease pairs reach Pathway-supported, 1
is Evidence-limited, and 8 are Not supported. Frozen-weight
transfer preserves AUROC> 0.93 for all diseases.

on pathway conclusions in matched-control audit design; the

classifiers. The protocol requires that (i) targeted perturba￾tions are compared against anatomically matched controls,
(ii) the perturbation operator is documented and compared
via a preregistered operator-comparison battery, (iii) path￾way specificity is re-tested under frozen-weight transfer to

pair, constraining interpretation under operator dependence

> 高性能 ECG 分类器不一定使用疾病一致的证据；只有把目标通路和 matched anatomical controls 比较，并经过外部迁移与算子敏感性检查，才能判断 pathway-specific evidence 是否成立。

下面给你一个可直接执行的修改方案。

---

# 一、Abstract 总体修改目标

## 现在的问题

目前 Abstract 的主要问题是：

1. **Results 数字太密**：CRBBB/CLBBB、SBRAD、AFIB 都列了多组 ASS 数值，信息量过载。
2. **故事线不够突出**：读者需要自己从结果中提炼 “1AVB 证明 matched control 必要、BBB 是稳定阳性、AFIB 是 operator artifact、SBRAD 是架构依赖”。
3. **方法贡献被细节稀释**：matched-control audit、operator comparison、external transfer、evidence tiering 都写了，但没有形成一个特别强的 methodological claim。
4. **Conclusion 可以更锋利**：应该更明确地说，这个 audit 改变了对高性能模型的解释：有些疾病高 AUROC 但 pathway-unsupported。

---

# 二、建议采用的新结构

建议 Abstract 分成四段，保持 Background / Methods / Results / Conclusions，但每段只承担一个任务。

---

## 1. Background：把核心缺口说得更尖锐

### 现在的问题

现在 Background 讲了 “high discrimination may rely on irrelevant regions”，这是对的，但还可以更明确地区分：

- perturbation sensitivity：某个区域被扰动后模型性能下降；
- pathway specificity：疾病预期区域比 matched controls 更重要。

### 建议写法重点

Background 应该突出一句：

> Existing perturbation explanations often test whether a region matters, but pathway claims require showing that the disease-relevant region matters more than matched anatomical controls.

也就是把 “sensitivity is not specificity” 变成摘要的逻辑核心，而不是一句附带评论。

---

## 2. Methods：少列组件，多讲判据

### 现在的问题

Methods 段现在把很多设计都放进去了：linear interpolation、external transfer、operator battery、evidence rules、five diagnoses、four architectures、two datasets。内容对，但太满。

### 建议保留四个核心点

Methods 只需要说清：

1. 预定义 disease-relevant target pathway；
2. 设计 matched anatomical controls；
3. 用 ASS 衡量 target 是否超过 strongest control；
4. 在 CODE 内部和 PTB-XL frozen-weight transfer 外部验证，并检查 operator dependence。

其他如 “five diagnoses spanning timing/morphology/rhythm”、“four architectures” 可以保留，但不要写太细。

---

## 3. Results：按证据类型组织，而不是按疾病堆数字

### 现在的问题

Results 现在基本是把 Table X 压缩进摘要。数字很多，但读者不容易抓住层级。

### 建议 Results 的顺序

建议按这个顺序写：

#### 第一，1AVB：方法必要性的 anchor case

这是最重要的 methodological result。  
要保留代表性数字：

- PR perturbation 有明显 AUROC drop；
- 但 matched QRS control 更强；
- ResNet internal ASS 为负，external ASS 也为负。

不需要列所有架构，只需要说明 all raw-signal architectures consistent。

#### 第二，operator comparison：说明 zero-masking artifact

这支撑为什么 linear interpolation 是 primary operator。  
可以保留一句：

> The operator-comparison battery showed that zero-masking inflated control-region disruption and could reverse pathway conclusions; linear interpolation was therefore used for primary tiering.

#### 第三，BBB：稳定阳性结果

CRBBB/CLBBB 是最强 positive result。  
这里不需要列 6 个具体 external ASS，最多写：

> CRBBB and CLBBB reached Pathway-supported on all three raw-signal architectures, with positive internal and external ASS CIs.

如果要保留数字，可以只写范围：

> external ASS range: CRBBB 0.255–0.455; CLBBB 0.261–0.387.

#### 第四，SBRAD 和 AFIB：异质性和伪影

SBRAD：ResNet evidence-limited，另外两个 not supported。  
AFIB：linear interpolation 下全部 negative，zero-masking positive 是 artifact。

#### 第五，总结 tier count

保留：

> 6/15 Pathway-supported, 1/15 Evidence-limited, 8/15 Not supported.

这是很好的总结数字，应该保留。

---

## 4. Conclusions：强调“高性能 ≠ 通路证据”

Conclusion 建议更明确地写成：

> High discrimination did not imply pathway-specific evidence. The audit separated disease-consistent signal use from correlated signal use and operator artifacts.

下面给你一个我建议的重写版本，风格尽量保持 IEEE/JBHI 摘要风格。

## Revised Abstract Draft

**Abstract—Background:** ECG classifiers often achieve high discrimination, but high AUROC does not establish that decisions are based on disease-consistent signal pathways. Existing perturbation explanations commonly test whether a region is influential, but pathway claims require anatomical specificity: the disease-relevant region should be more disruptive than matched control regions.

**Methods:** We propose a model-agnostic matched-control pathway audit for ECG classifiers. For each diagnosis, we prespecified a clinically expected target pathway and anatomically adjacent controls, quantified pathway specificity using the Anatomical Specificity Score (ASS; target ∆AUROC minus the strongest control ∆AUROC), and evaluated whether conclusions transferred under frozen weights from CODE-15% to cardiologist-validated PTB-XL fold 10. A preregistered operator-comparison battery assessed perturbation-operator dependence and motivated linear interpolation as the primary continuity-preserving operator. The audit was applied to five diagnoses spanning timing, morphology, and rhythm pathways across ResNet, SE-ResNet, Transformer, and supporting XGBoost feature-space models.

**Results:** All raw-signal models achieved high discrimination, but pathway evidence diverged sharply from AUROC. 1AVB served as the anchor failure case: PR-window perturbation caused a large AUROC drop, yet matched QRS perturbation was more disruptive, yielding negative ASS internally and externally. Thus, PR sensitivity did not imply PR specificity. The operator-comparison battery showed that zero-masking introduced boundary artifacts and could reverse pathway conclusions. Under the primary linear-interpolation operator, QRS-morphology pathways for CRBBB and CLBBB were Pathway-supported on all three raw-signal architectures, with positive internal and external ASS. SBRAD showed architecture-dependent evidence: ResNet was Evidence-limited, whereas SE-ResNet and Transformer were Not supported. AFIB atrial-window ASS was negative across all architectures and both datasets, reclassifying the initial zero-masking positive as an operator artifact. Overall, 6 of 15 model-disease pairs were Pathway-supported, 1 was Evidence-limited, and 8 were Not supported. Frozen-weight transfer preserved AUROC > 0.93 for all diseases.

**Conclusions:** High discrimination alone was insufficient to infer disease-consistent signal use. The matched-control audit, combined with explicit operator documentation and external transfer, separated stable pathway-specific evidence from correlated signal use and perturbation artifacts. This framework may generalize to other biomedical signal domains where clinically expected input regions can be specified a priori, although current evidence is limited to five ECG diagnoses across two datasets.

I. INTRODUCTION
Deep learning classifiers for electrocardiogram (ECG) anal￾ysis now achieve high discrimination across a growing set of
cardiac conditions [1]–[4], aided by large public datasets such
as PTB-XL [5] and CODE-15% [6]. But strong discrimination
does not tell us whether a model relies on disease-relevant
signal regions—a gap that matters for clinical deployment
beyond benchmark performance. A 1AVB classifier might
depend on QRS morphology instead of PR-interval timing; an
AFIB classifier might use ventricular rate irregularity, atrial
waveform features, or unrelated shortcuts. Standard bench￾mark metrics cannot distinguish these cases. Moreover, exist￾ing explanation methods rarely test whether disease-relevant
regions dominate over matched controls, or whether pathway
dependence holds up under dataset shift—sensitivity is not
specificity, and explanation conclusions can be fragile under
distribution shift [7], [8].
We address these gaps with a model-agnostic, matched￾control perturbation audit protocol. For each diagnosis we pre￾specify an expected positive pathway (e.g., the PR segment
for 1AVB, the QRS complex for bundle branch block) and
compare targeted perturbations against anatomically adjacent
control regions that should matter less. A pathway claim is
accepted only if the target perturbation is more disruptive
than its strongest matched control—a stricter criterion than
perturbation sensitivity alone. We further evaluate pathway
specificity under frozen-weight transfer from CODE-15% to
cardiologist-validated PTB-XL fold 10, providing an external
check on whether explanation conclusions are dataset-specific.
The protocol is model-agnostic: the same perturbation design
applies to any classifier accepting 12-lead ECG input, and
the five diseases are a case-study panel chosen to span three
diagnostic pathway categories (timing, morphology, rhythm),
not an exhaustive clinical survey.

We instantiate the audit across four model architectures
(XGBoost, ResNet, SE-ResNet, and a lightweight Trans￾former) at three representation levels—simple summary fea￾tures, timing-enriched handcrafted features, and raw signal—
to assess whether pathway dependence is consistent across

evaluated internally on CODE-15% (345,779 exams, patient￾level split) and externally on PTB-XL fold 10 (cardiologist￾validated labels).
Our primary contribution is the audit protocol itself—a
structured method for evaluating whether ECG classifiers base
decisions on disease-relevant signal regions, rather than on
correlated but clinically non-specific features. We show that
a matched-control design with external transfer can separate
pathway claims that remain anatomically specific and exter￾nally consistent from those that do not, and can identify cases
where target perturbation alone would produce misleading
conclusions. The protocol also reveals that the perturbation
operator itself is a critical methodological variable: zero￾masking, the most common occlusion method in the lit￾erature, creates hard-boundary artifacts that inflate control￾region disruption and can reverse specificity conclusions. A
continuity-preserving operator (linear interpolation) eliminates
this artifact and provides more conservative, anatomically

gap between standard discrimination benchmarks (which mea￾sure only predictive accuracy) and pathway-specific evidence
(which requires evidence about how models arrive at deci￾sions).
II. RELATED WORK
A. ECG Classification with Deep Learning
1D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and residual
architectures have become the dominant paradigm for auto￾mated ECG classification. Hannun et al. [1] demonstrated
cardiologist-level arrhythmia detection using a 34-layer 1D
CNN on ambulatory ECGs. On the PTB-XL benchmark,
Strodthoff et al. [2] established strong baselines with 1D
ResNets and fully convolutional networks across 71 diagnostic
classes; their follow-up review [3] confirmed that ResNet-style
architectures remain competitive against newer alternatives.
Mehari and Strodthoff [9] further advanced PTB-XL bench￾marks through self-supervised pre-training, while Chen et
al. [10] and Zubair et al. [11] contributed targeted architectures
for multi-class and imbalanced ECG classification.
Beyond vanilla ResNets, SE-ResNet [12] adds channel-wise
attention, and lightweight Transformer adaptations [13] have
been applied via patch-based self-attention. Recent hybrid
architectures combine these paradigms—Cardioformer [14]
couples multi-granularity patching with Transformer layers,
while xECGArch [15] separates morphology and rhythm pro￾cessing with dual CNNs. ECG-JEPA [16] pushed PTB-XL
performance to AUROC=0.945 through JEPA pre-training
on over one million records spanning ten datasets including
CODE-15%. Foundation models such as ECG-FM [17] fur￾ther scale pre-training, though their explanation behavior and
pathway-level auditability remain unexplored. Prior to the deep
learning era, classical machine learning methods—including
XGBoost, random forests, and support vector machines—
were widely applied to handcrafted ECG features and remain
competitive baselines on structured feature sets [18], [19].
Despite these advances across both classical and deep
learning paradigms, the common evaluation framework em￾phasizes discrimination metrics on held-out test splits. It
remains unclear whether these models base their decisions
on disease-relevant signal regions, and whether region-specific
dependence survives cross-dataset transfer. This gap motivates
our multi-level audit protocol, which applies identical pathway
questions across representation levels—from a feature-based
XGBoost baseline to a raw-signal ResNet—allowing us to
assess pathway dependence across both classical and deep
learning models.
B. Explainability and Perturbation Methods
Post-hoc explanation methods—including saliency maps,
occlusion-based sensitivity, guided backpropagation, and in￾tegrated gradients—have been systematically evaluated on
ECG tasks. Storas et al. [20] compared nine gradient-based ˚
methods on synthetic 12-lead ECGs and found that no single
method works best across all measurement tasks, with con￾siderable disagreement between human expert evaluation and
perturbation-based metrics. Suh et al. [21] evaluated eleven
attribution methods across five large ECG datasets and re￾ported that Guided Grad-CAM best aligned with cardiologists’
assessment while localization-based metrics better reflected
human judgment than perturbation-based ones. Plagwitz et
al. [22] assessed the reliability of feature attribution explana￾tions in ECG analysis through systematic perturbation testing,
reporting that explanation reliability varies substantially across
attribution methods and disease categories. Al-Zaiti et al. [23]
found that clinically deployed saliency maps for occlusion
MI detection were rated only slightly clinically relevant by
practicing clinicians, underscoring the gap between current
explanation quality and clinical expectations.
Perturbation-based evaluation—in which input regions are
removed or altered to measure prediction change—provides
a more direct test of feature dependence than gradient-based
attributions alone. Wagner et al. [24] proposed a structured
XAI framework for ECG that combines occlusion-based san￾ity checks, glocal attribution aggregation, and concept-based
analysis, providing quantitative evidence that model behav￾ior can align with cardiologists’ decision rules. Bender et
al. [25] demonstrated that a ResNet trained for 12-lead ECG
classification learns features analogous to clinical diagnostic
criteria including P-wave morphology, QRS duration, and
PR interval. Recent work has also applied wave masking
and reconstruction-based perturbation strategies [26], [27],
and Shapley-value-based ablation [28] to quantify localized
feature importance in ECG classifiers. Beyond ECG, Ross
et al. [29] demonstrated that constraining models to produce
“right” explanations during training can improve generaliza￾tion, providing an alternative to post-hoc auditing—though
their approach requires ground-truth explanation annotations
that are rarely available for clinical ECG tasks.

Despite these advances, three structural limitations persist
across the existing ECG explanation literature. First, existing
perturbation studies rarely incorporate matched anatomical
controls: they test whether a region matters, but not whether
disease-specific regions matter more than adjacent control
regions. This is the key distinction between perturbation
sensitivity (a region is important) and anatomical specificity (a
disease-specific region is more important than its anatomically
adjacent controls)—a distinction we operationalize through the
ASS metric and matched-control design. Second, explanation
conclusions are typically validated only within the training
distribution. Adebayo et al. [7] showed that saliency maps
can fail basic sanity checks under simple input transfor￾mations, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola [30] demonstrated that
interpretability methods can be fragile under input pertur￾bations, and Ong Ly et al. [31] demonstrated that hidden
data acquisition biases in ECG datasets can inflate model
performance by up to 20%, with AUROC dropping from 0.90
to 0.70 under external validation. In medical imaging more
broadly, DeGrave et al. [32] showed that deep learning models
for radiographic COVID-19 detection selected clinically irrele￾vant shortcuts over meaningful signal—a finding that directly
parallels our concern about ECG classifiers exploiting non￾specific waveform features. Third, few studies test whether
explanation claims survive external dataset shift [8]. These
gaps directly motivate our matched-control perturbation design
with frozen-weight cross-dataset transfer.
C. Dataset Use and Cross-Dataset Validation
The two largest public 12-lead ECG datasets—PTB-XL [5]
(21,837 records, cardiologist-validated labels) and CODE-15%
[6] (345,779 exams, automated labels)—have enabled a wide
range of deep learning studies. PTB-XL provides carefully
annotated multi-label diagnoses with rich metadata including
signal quality indicators and demographic attributes, while
CODE-15% offers an order of magnitude more samples but
with labels derived from an automated interpretation system.
This label-source asymmetry introduces a critical distinction:
models trained on CODE-15% may learn to replicate the
automated labeling logic rather than physician-level diagnostic
features, creating a label circularity risk that varies by disease
category. The PTB-XL+ dataset [33] supplements PTB-XL
with 71 handcrafted features spanning heart rate variability,
QRS morphology, and signal quality metrics, enabling direct
comparisons between learned representations and classical
ECG parameters.
Cross-dataset validation remains underutilized in the ECG
deep learning literature, and where it has been attempted,
the results are sobering. Bickmann et al. [18] benchmarked
time-series versus feature-based methods on PTB-XL but
did not include external validation. Soltanieh et al. [34]
addressed out-of-distribution generalization for self-supervised
ECG representations, showing that dataset shift degrades stan￾dard supervised baselines. Frank et al. [35] reported that
models achieving AUROC>0.90 within-dataset for myocardial
ischemia detection experienced substantial performance drops
across six public ECG databases. At the foundation-model
scale, ECGFounder [36] and recent benchmarking efforts [37]
confirm that cross-domain generalization remains a key chal￾lenge even for large pre-trained models with diverse training
data.
The consistent picture is that external validation across
datasets with different label sources, populations, and acqui￾sition protocols is widely recommended but rarely executed,
and even less often applied to explanation claims. Our study
addresses this gap through frozen-weight transfer from CODE￾15% to cardiologist-validated PTB-XL fold 10, treating the
external dataset as a simultaneous check on both prediction
quality and pathway explanation consistency.
D. Clinical Pathway and Mechanistic Analysis
Clinical ECG interpretation relies on well-defined phys￾iological features: PR interval for atrioventricular conduc￾tion timing, QRS duration and morphology for ventricular
conduction, RR interval regularity for rhythm classification,
and P-wave morphology for atrial activity assessment [38].
These features define distinct diagnostic pathways for condi￾tions such as 1AVB (prolonged PR>200ms), bundle branch
blocks (wide QRS>120ms with characteristic terminal/lateral
R patterns), sinus bradycardia (low ventricular rate), and atrial
fibrillation (absent or fibrillatory atrial activity).
Recent studies have directly tested whether deep ECG
models learn these clinically meaningful features. Hempel et
al. [39] extended an XAI framework to match deep learning
relevances with PR interval and QRS duration from PTB-XL+,
reporting that 96.0% of high-confidence 1AVB predictions had
PR>200ms and 98.6% of high-confidence LBBB predictions
had QRS>120ms—strong evidence that the model internally
represents clinical thresholds. Riberg et al. [40] performed a
concordance analysis between ResNet predictions and cardi￾ology guideline thresholds, finding that RR interval features
dominated for sinus bradycardia and tachycardia while mor￾phological features showed weaker correlation. Hammer et
al. [41] introduced an architecture that explicitly separates
rhythm (long-term) and morphology (short-term) processing,
demonstrating that fused explanations correlate with clinical
diagnostic criteria. A systematic review by Ayano et al. [42]
confirmed that interpretable ML studies for ECG increasingly
target clinical parameters such as PR interval, QRS duration,
and RR variability.
Despite this progress, a critical gap remains: existing studies
confirm that models attend to clinically relevant features,
but they do not test whether a disease-specific signal region
dominates over anatomically adjacent controls, or whether
such pathway specificity survives dataset shift. Demonstrating
feature relevance is not the same as demonstrating feature
specificity. Our disease-centered, matched-control perturbation
audit addresses this gap: for five diagnoses spanning timing,
morphology, and rhythm pathways, we pre-specify expected
positive regions grounded in clinical physiology, compare
targeted perturbations against matched controls, and verify
pathway specificity under frozen-weight external transfer. This
design transforms clinical pathway knowledge into testable,
falsifiable audit criteria.

III. METHODS
A. Dataset
CODE-15%: Brazilian ECG dataset with 345,779 12-lead
exams (400Hz, 10-second duration) from 233,770 patients.
We use five target conditions because they span three distinct
diagnostic pathways: 1AVB (timing), CRBBB/CLBBB (mor￾phology), and SBRAD/AFIB (rhythm). Their prevalences are
1.65%, 2.80%, 1.74%, 1.62%, and 2.03%, respectively.
Label source and circularity risk: Labels were derived
from the CODE dataset’s automated ECG interpretation sys￾tem. CODE serves as an automated-label internal audit cohort.
The risk of label circularity—where the model reproduces the
automated labeling logic instead of recovering physician-level
diagnostic mechanisms—varies by disease:
• 1AVB—Highest risk: The label definition (PR>200ms)
and PR-interval proxy features overlap heavily, so models
may learn the automated threshold instead of clinical AV￾conduction features.
• SBRAD—High risk: Heart-rate-based rules
(HR<60bpm) directly overlap with the label source,
making learned rate-threshold behavior hard to
distinguish from label replication.
• CRBBB/CLBBB—Moderate risk: QRS morphology
criteria (width >120ms, terminal R′
/broad R patterns)
may align with the automated interpretation system’s
feature extraction.
• AFIB—Moderate risk: P-wave absence and atrial activ￾ity metrics may overlap with the rhythm classifier com￾ponent of the automated system, though RR irregularity
alone provides only a partial signal.
To buffer these risks, we treat PTB-XL fold 10 (cardiologist￾validated labels) as the primary external validation, and we
recommend interpreting internal CODE findings as evidence
about model behavior relative to the existing automated￾label system, not as evidence of physician-level diagnostic
reasoning.
Patient-level split: 60% train (207,232 samples), 20% vali￾dation (69,045 samples), 20% test (69,520 samples). Random
seed 42 for reproducibility. Patient-level splitting ensures no
patient appears in multiple splits, preventing leakage from
patient-specific patterns.
B. Disease-Centered Finding Map and Audit Panel
The audit framework is built around a compact, literature￾guided finding map covering five diagnoses: 1AVB, CRBBB,
CLBBB, SBRAD, and AFIB. For each disease we pre-specify
(i) the expected positive pathway, (ii) matched negative/control
regions that should produce smaller effects, and (iii) any
ambiguous pathway treated as hypothesis-testing. The map is
intentionally compact and disease-centered.
SBRAD now contributes matched pathway audits on both
CODE and PTB-XL via rate normalization with QRS and ST
controls, so it enters pathway-score aggregation as a narrower
cross-dataset audit case. AFIB is handled differently from the
outset: RR irregularity alone is an explicit ambiguity test.
Clinical anchoring. Each target region and control pairing
is grounded in established ECG diagnostic criteria [38]. The
target window maps to the clinically accepted diagnostic
feature for that disease (PR prolongation for 1AVB, QRS
widening for BBB, low ventricular rate for SBRAD, absent
P-waves for AFIB). Each matched control is anatomically
adjacent to the target and involves a physiologically distinct
structure (e.g., ST segment vs PR interval, QRS complex vs
atrial window), ensuring that the control perturbation tests
a plausible alternative signal channel rather than a trivially
irrelevant region. This design ensures that a positive ASS
reflects genuine anatomical specificity: the target pathway is
more important than its most disruptive anatomically adjacent
alternative.
C. The Audit Protocol as a Model-Agnostic Method
The audit protocol is designed to be model-agnostic:
the same perturbation windows, matched-control compar￾isons, and evaluation metrics apply to any classifier that
accepts 12-lead ECG input, regardless of architecture (con￾volutional, transformer-based, tree-based, or hybrid). The five
diagnoses—1AVB, CRBBB, CLBBB, SBRAD, and AFIB—
serve as a case-study panel chosen to span three clinically
distinct diagnostic pathway categories (timing, morphology,
rhythm), and are not intended as an exhaustive clinical survey.
The protocol itself does not depend on the specific diseases,
the model architecture, or the training dataset. We demon￾strate this model-agnostic property by instantiating the audit
across four architectures (XGBoost, ResNet, SE-ResNet, and a
lightweight Transformer) and three representation levels, with
external validation on an independent cardiologist-validated
dataset.
D. Supporting Models and Representation Ladder

choice [12], [13].

Summary Features (98D)

(Mean/Std/Min/Max/Median/Range), HR (Mean/Std),
HRV (RMSSD/SDNN/pNN50/CV), RR Irregularity,
QRS Count
• Amplitude features (84): Per-lead statistics
(Mean/Std/Min/Max/Range/RMS/PeakToPeak) for
12 leads

how far rhythm and coarse amplitude summaries can go before

Recent work has also applied wave masking
and reconstruction-based perturbation strategies [26], [27],
and Shapley-value-based ablation [28] to quantify localized
feature importance in ECG classifiers. Beyond ECG, Ross
et al. [29] demonstrated that constraining models to produce
“right” explanations during training can improve generaliza￾tion, providing an alternative to post-hoc auditing—though
their approach requires ground-truth explanation annotations
that are rarely available for clinical ECG tasks.IEEE JOURNAL OF BIOMEDICAL AND HEALTH INFORMATICS, VOL. XX, NO. XX, MONTH 2025 3
Despite these advances, three structural limitations persist
across the existing ECG explanation literature. First, existing
perturbation studies rarely incorporate matched anatomical
controls: they test whether a region matters, but not whether
disease-specific regions matter more than adjacent control
regions. This is the key distinction between perturbation
sensitivity (a region is important) and anatomical specificity (a
disease-specific region is more important than its anatomically
adjacent controls)—a distinction we operationalize through the
ASS metric and matched-control design. Second, explanation
conclusions are typically validated only within the training
distribution. Adebayo et al. [7] showed that saliency maps
can fail basic sanity checks under simple input transfor￾mations, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola [30] demonstrated that
interpretability methods can be fragile under input pertur￾bations, and Ong Ly et al. [31] demonstrated that hidden
data acquisition biases in ECG datasets can inflate model
performance by up to 20%, with AUROC dropping from 0.90
to 0.70 under external validation. In medical imaging more
broadly, DeGrave et al. [32] showed that deep learning models
for radiographic COVID-19 detection selected clinically irrele￾vant shortcuts over meaningful signal—a finding that directly
parallels our concern about ECG classifiers exploiting non￾specific waveform features. Third, few studies test whether
explanation claims survive external dataset shift [8]. These
gaps directly motivate our matched-control perturbation design
with frozen-weight cross-dataset transfer.
C. Dataset Use and Cross-Dataset Validation
The two largest public 12-lead ECG datasets—PTB-XL [5]
(21,837 records, cardiologist-validated labels) and CODE-15%
[6] (345,779 exams, automated labels)—have enabled a wide
range of deep learning studies. PTB-XL provides carefully
annotated multi-label diagnoses with rich metadata including
signal quality indicators and demographic attributes, while
CODE-15% offers an order of magnitude more samples but
with labels derived from an automated interpretation system.
This label-source asymmetry introduces a critical distinction:
models trained on CODE-15% may learn to replicate the
automated labeling logic rather than physician-level diagnostic
features, creating a label circularity risk that varies by disease
category. The PTB-XL+ dataset [33] supplements PTB-XL
with 71 handcrafted features spanning heart rate variability,
QRS morphology, and signal quality metrics, enabling direct
comparisons between learned representations and classical
ECG parameters.
Cross-dataset validation remains underutilized in the ECG
deep learning literature, and where it has been attempted,
the results are sobering. Bickmann et al. [18] benchmarked
time-series versus feature-based methods on PTB-XL but

6) No subgroup or fairness analysis: We did not evaluate
performance by age, sex, site, device, or recording
quality, and no fairness claims should be inferred from
the present results.
7) Patient-level splitting without patient-level aggrega￾tion analysis: We prevented leakage through patient￾level splitting, but did not study patient-level aggregation
strategies when multiple ECGs per patient are available.
8) Statistical inference with patient-level clustering: The
permutation tests and DeLong comparisons reported in
the Results use sample-level inference (n ≈ 69, 500
ECGs from ≈ 47, 000 unique patients). Because within￾patient correlations are not modeled, the effective de￾grees of freedom are closer to the number of unique
patients than to the number of ECGs. Patient-clustered
bootstrap for AUROC differences or a cluster-robust
variance estimator for DeLong tests would provide more
conservative inference. As a practical sensitivity check,
we recommend that readers treat the patient-level boot￾strap CIs (not the permutation p-values) as the primary
uncertainty quantification, and we defer formal cluster￾adjusted inference to future work.
9) Metadata and acquisition confounding remain pos￾sible: Differences in devices, acquisition pipelines, and
other unmodeled dataset characteristics may contribute
to both internal performance patterns and external trans￾fer gaps.
10) Limited to 5 cardiac conditions: Many other ECG
diagnoses not evaluated.
11) No cardiologist review: Manual inspection of failure
cases would strengthen clinical interpretation.
12) Hybrid models unexplored: Combining Clinical-MVP
features with learned representations may offer further
improvements.IEEE JOURNAL OF BIOMEDICAL AND HEALTH INFORMATICS, VOL. XX, NO. XX, MONTH 2025 22
G. Future Work
Several directions merit further investigation. The cross￾architecture perturbation audit (Section IV-C) has been com￾pleted on CODE-15%; extending it to the external PTB￾XL dataset under linear interpolation would reveal whether
architecture-dependent ASS patterns survive dataset shift.
Validation on additional independent datasets across differ￾ent continents, devices, and populations is needed to es￾tablish generalizability. A dedicated cardiologist-adjudicated
subset of CODE-15% remains important for formal label￾noise quantification. Lead-stratified perturbation experiments
with clinician review of failure cases would add anatomical
granularity beyond the current all-lead protocol. Extending
the audit panel to more diagnoses, incorporating subgroup
and fairness analyses, and evaluating hybrid models that
combine handcrafted features with learned representations
are natural next steps. More realistic perturbation designs—
including physiologically motivated simulations instead of
signal removal—could strengthen mechanistic interpretation.
Finally, the operator-comparison battery findings demonstrate
that perturbation operator choice is an important influence
on pathway conclusions in matched-control audit design; the
broader perturbation literature would benefit from community
standards on operator selection, preregistration, and mini￾mal reporting requirements for perturbation-based explanation
studies.

Interpretation boundaries. To clarify what the current
audit design can and cannot support, we distinguish four levels
of evidence:
1) Pathway sensitivity: Perturbation of the target region
causes a performance drop.
2) Pathway specificity: The target-region drop exceeds the
drop from matched control perturbations (ASS> 0).
3) Mechanistic validity: The model uses the same physi￾ological mechanisms that clinicians employ.
4) Clinical validity: The mechanism holds under physician
annotation or predicts real clinical outcomes.
The audit conclusions in this paper are structured around
pathway sensitivity and specificity (levels 1–2). Claims about
mechanistic or clinical validity (levels 3–4) require additional
evidence—clinician review of failure cases, formal mediation
analysis, or prospective validation—that is beyond the scope of
this study. This audit supports evidence plausibility under a
controlled perturbation protocol, not mechanistic causality
or clinical utility. Pathway-supported designations indicate
that a model’s predictions are more sensitive to disease￾relevant than to control-region perturbation under a primary
operator; they do not certify that the model uses the same
physiological mechanisms as a clinician, nor that the model is
safe for deployment.
Patient-level splitting, multi-seed training, and compre￾hensive metrics are essential protocol-level practices that
prevent data leakage, confirm training stability (within-split
SD= 0.0025), and capture the full performance picture beyond
a single metric. The representation ladder confirms that feature
complementarity operates across three axes (rhythm, morphol￾ogy, timing), and that explicit proxy features can recover
clinically relevant signal without end-to-end learning.IEEE JOURNAL OF BIOMEDICAL AND HEALTH INFORMATICS, VOL. XX, NO. XX, MONTH 2025 21
F. Limitations
1) Single external validation dataset: Frozen-model val￾idation was performed on PTB-XL (21k samples,
German population), providing evidence for model￾level generalization (Section IV-D, strict frozen Micro￾F1=0.571). The 3-level transfer framework (strict frozen
0.571 / target-domain threshold retuning 0.681 / optimal
0.694) provides transparent bounds on frozen-model
transfer. However, validation on additional independent
datasets (different continents, devices, and populations)
is needed to establish generalizability. We note that
the Level-2 (calibrated) threshold retuning uses PTB￾XL fold 9, which contains automated (not human￾adjudicated) labels, potentially introducing a separate
source of label noise into the operating-point adaptation
step. PTB-XL fold 10 is cardiologist-validated (n =
2, 198), while all CODE-15% labels and PTB-XL folds
1–9 labels are automated.
2) Automated labels, not physician-confirmed: CODE￾15% labels derive from automated ECG interpretation,
not cardiologist adjudication. This introduces label noise
that could affect both training and evaluation. PTB￾XL fold 10 provides a cardiologist-validated credibil￾ity buffer, but does not fully eliminate the possibility
that internal CODE findings remain partly aligned with
the original automated labeling logic. We therefore
treat internal analyses as audit-relative, not physician￾equivalent.

F. Confirmatory Inference: Clustered Bootstrap and Multiplic￾ity Control
The primary external audit tests 15 pre-specified hypotheses
of the form H0 : ASS ≤ 0 (one-sided) under the primary

within-patient correlation and multiplicity, we apply two com￾plementary safeguards.
Patient-clustered bootstrap. All confidence intervals and
Pr(ASS> 0) values are computed via patient-level cluster
bootstrap (1,000 replicates, seed 42). In each replicate, patients
(not individual ECGs) are resampled with replacement; all
ECGs belonging to a resampled patient are included, preserv￾ing the within-patient correlation structure. ASS is computed
on the paired target-versus-control perturbation effects within
each replicate, maintaining the matched-subject design. The
reported Pr(ASS> 0) is the fraction of bootstrap replicates in
which the replicate ASS exceeds zero, providing a bootstrap￾based one-sided p-value for H0 : ASS ≤ 0.
Multiplicity control. The 15 external tests constitute a
single confirmatory family. We apply the Benjamini–Hochberg
false discovery rate (BH-FDR) procedure at α = 0.05 to
control the expected proportion of false positives among
rejected hypotheses. Table XII reports the bootstrap p-values,
BH-FDR thresholds, and Storey q-values for all 15 pairs.

VI. CONCLUSION
We propose a model-agnostic matched-control pathway au￾dit protocol for evaluating pathway-specific evidence in ECG
classifiers. The protocol requires that (i) targeted perturba￾tions are compared against anatomically matched controls,
(ii) the perturbation operator is documented and compared
via a preregistered operator-comparison battery, (iii) path￾way specificity is re-tested under frozen-weight transfer to
an independent cardiologist-validated dataset, and (iv) per￾model evidence tiers—pathway-supported, evidence-limited,
not supported—are assigned to each (architecture, disease)
pair, constraining interpretation under operator dependence
and external transfer without aggregating across architectures.
Applied to five diagnoses as a case-study panel, the protocol
reveals heterogeneity invisible to discrimination metrics alone:
1AVB is Not supported across all three architectures on
both datasets—a replicated matched-control failure demon￾strating that target-only perturbation can produce false-positive
pathway claims; CRBBB and CLBBB both reach Pathway￾supported on all three architectures (internal+external positive
ASS with CI> 0 on both datasets, CDDC= 1.0 for all
6 pairs), confirming that QRS-morphology pathway speci￾ficity is architecture-invariant and dataset-invariant; SBRAD
splits—ResNet Evidence-limited (rate-pathway positive inter￾nally and externally but external CI narrowly crosses zero),
SE-ResNet and Transformer Not supported—demonstrating
that rate-pathway learning is architecture-dependent; AFIB is
Not supported on all three architectures on both datasets, with
its earlier zero-masking positive revealed as operator artifact.
Overall, 6 of 15 model-disease pairs reach Pathway-supported,
1 is Evidence-limited, and 8 are Not supported. The sole
Evidence-limited designation (SBRAD-ResNet) reflects nar￾row CI margin, not absent external data or protocol failure. A
preregistered operator-comparison battery shows that operator
choice strongly influences pathway conclusions: zero-masking
creates boundary artifacts that can reverse specificity, while
linear interpolation provides more interpretable behavior. The
CRBBB case is instructive: zero-masking produced the appear￾ance of external pathway failure (PTB-XL ASS−0.023Z
), but
the primary operator reveals robust external pathway speci￾ficity (ASS 0.455L
)—demonstrating that operator selection
is a necessary precondition for pathway-specificity claims.
Standard discrimination metrics (AUROC> 0.98 for all five
diseases) are insufficient for evaluating whether a classifier
uses disease-consistent signal pathways under this audit. The
matched-control audit principle, combined with operator se￾lection and external transfer, may extend to other biomedical
signal domains where clinically relevant input regions can be
defined a priori, though the current evidence is limited to five
ECG diagnoses on two datasets.

Recent work has also applied wave masking
and reconstruction-based perturbation strategies [26], [27],
and Shapley-value-based ablation [28] to quantify localized
feature importance in ECG classifiers. Beyond ECG, Ross
et al. [29] demonstrated that constraining models to produce
“right” explanations during training can improve generaliza￾tion, providing an alternative to post-hoc auditing—though
their approach requires ground-truth explanation annotations
that are rarely available for clinical ECG tasks.IEEE JOURNAL OF BIOMEDICAL AND HEALTH INFORMATICS, VOL. XX, NO. XX, MONTH 2025 3
Despite these advances, three structural limitations persist
across the existing ECG explanation literature. First, existing
perturbation studies rarely incorporate matched anatomical
controls: they test whether a region matters, but not whether
disease-specific regions matter more than adjacent control
regions. This is the key distinction between perturbation
sensitivity (a region is important) and anatomical specificity (a
disease-specific region is more important than its anatomically
adjacent controls)—a distinction we operationalize through the
ASS metric and matched-control design. Second, explanation
conclusions are typically validated only within the training
distribution. Adebayo et al. [7] showed that saliency maps
can fail basic sanity checks under simple input transfor￾mations, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola [30] demonstrated that
interpretability methods can be fragile under input pertur￾bations, and Ong Ly et al. [31] demonstrated that hidden
data acquisition biases in ECG datasets can inflate model
performance by up to 20%, with AUROC dropping from 0.90
to 0.70 under external validation. In medical imaging more
broadly, DeGrave et al. [32] showed that deep learning models
for radiographic COVID-19 detection selected clinically irrele￾vant shortcuts over meaningful signal—a finding that directly
parallels our concern about ECG classifiers exploiting non￾specific waveform features. Third, few studies test whether
explanation claims survive external dataset shift [8]. These
gaps directly motivate our matched-control perturbation design
with frozen-weight cross-dataset transfer.
C. Dataset Use and Cross-Dataset Validation
The two largest public 12-lead ECG datasets—PTB-XL [5]
(21,837 records, cardiologist-validated labels) and CODE-15%
[6] (345,779 exams, automated labels)—have enabled a wide
range of deep learning studies. PTB-XL provides carefully
annotated multi-label diagnoses with rich metadata including
signal quality indicators and demographic attributes, while
CODE-15% offers an order of magnitude more samples but
with labels derived from an automated interpretation system.
This label-source asymmetry introduces a critical distinction:
models trained on CODE-15% may learn to replicate the
automated labeling logic rather than physician-level diagnostic
features, creating a label circularity risk that varies by disease
category. The PTB-XL+ dataset [33] supplements PTB-XL
with 71 handcrafted features spanning heart rate variability,
QRS morphology, and signal quality metrics, enabling direct
comparisons between learned representations and classical
ECG parameters.
Cross-dataset validation remains underutilized in the ECG
deep learning literature, and where it has been attempted,
the results are sobering. Bickmann et al. [18] benchmarked

0.571 / target-domain threshold retuning 0.681 / optimal
0.694) provides transparent bounds on frozen-model
transfer. However, validation on additional independent
datasets (different continents, devices, and populations)
is needed to establish generalizability. We note that
the Level-2 (calibrated) threshold retuning uses PTB-
XL fold 9, which contains automated (not human-
adjudicated) labels, potentially introducing a separate
source of label noise into the operating-point adaptation
step. PTB-XL fold 10 is cardiologist-validated (n =

1–9 labels are automated.

15% labels derive from automated ECG interpretation,
not cardiologist adjudication. This introduces label noise
that could affect both training and evaluation. PTB-
XL fold 10 provides a cardiologist-validated credibil-
ity buffer, but does not fully eliminate the possibility
that internal CODE findings remain partly aligned with
the original automated labeling logic. We therefore
treat internal analyses as audit-relative, not physician-
equivalent. The PR>200ms rule baseline using Neu-

sensitivity (0.873) but low specificity (0.515), while

ment (DeLong p < 10−6
) indicates that frozen trans-
fer is not reducible to a simple PR-interval threshold.

15% would enable formal label-noise quantification and
remains important future work.

comprehensive measurements: While we include PR-

phology, QT interval, ST-segment measurements, de-
tailed fiducial timing (P/QRS/T onset/offset), and for-

proxy pipeline into a clinical gold standard.

conservative to discriminate, and linear interpolation
provides the most interpretable behavior. While we

perturbation literature in general has not converged on a
single best practice. Readers should treat pathway speci-

datasets.

performance by age, sex, site, device, or recording
quality, and no fairness claims should be inferred from
the present results.

level splitting, but did not study patient-level aggregation
strategies when multiple ECGs per patient are available.

permutation tests and DeLong comparisons reported in
the Results use sample-level inference (n ≈ 69, 500
ECGs from ≈ 47, 000 unique patients). Because within-
patient correlations are not modeled, the effective de-
grees of freedom are closer to the number of unique
patients than to the number of ECGs. Patient-clustered
bootstrap for AUROC differences or a cluster-robust
variance estimator for DeLong tests would provide more
conservative inference. As a practical sensitivity check,
we recommend that readers treat the patient-level boot-
strap CIs (not the permutation p-values) as the primary
uncertainty quantification, and we defer formal cluster-
adjusted inference to future work.

sible: Differences in devices, acquisition pipelines, and
other unmodeled dataset characteristics may contribute
to both internal performance patterns and external trans-
fer gaps.
10) Limited to 5 cardiac conditions: Many other ECG
diagnoses not evaluated.
11) No cardiologist review: Manual inspection of failure
cases would strengthen clinical interpretation.
12) Hybrid models unexplored: Combining Clinical-MVP
features with learned representations may offer further
improvements.

parts:
下面按论文 **Discussion 章节原本的标题/子标题** 来梳理。Discussion 的整体作用不是重复 Results，而是把结果上升成方法学观点：**这篇论文真正想说的是，解释模型不能只看“扰动后性能掉不掉”，还要看目标通路是否强于 matched controls、是否跨数据集稳定、是否受扰动算子影响。**

---

# V. DISCUSSION

## A. What the Audit Protocol Reveals About Pathway-Specific Evidence  
## 审计协议揭示了什么样的通路特异性证据

这一节是 Discussion 的总起。它把 Results 中的所有结果重新解释为一个核心观点：

> pathway-specific evidence 不是疾病标签本身的固定属性，而是具体模型的属性。

也就是说，不能说“某个疾病一定用了某个通路”，而应该说“某个模型在某个疾病上是否表现出这个通路证据”。

论文分别讨论几个模型。

---

### ResNet  
### 1D 卷积 ResNet：主要审计对象

ResNet 是全文最主要的 audit model。Discussion 中再次强调 1AVB 是核心示范：PR-window perturbation 的效果很大、也很符合医学直觉，但 matched QRS control 更强，所以 ASS 为负。这说明 **target-only perturbation 不足以支持 pathway claim**。fileciteturn10file2

同时，ResNet 也展示了 operator choice 的重要性。CLBBB 的 ASS 会随扰动算子改变方向，因此论文最终采用 linear interpolation，把 zero-masking 降级为 deprecated operator。fileciteturn10file2

在 ResNet 上，最终结论是：

| Disease-pathway | ResNet 结论 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| CRBBB / QRS morphology | Pathway-supported | QRS 通路内外部均成立 |
| CLBBB / QRS morphology | Pathway-supported | QRS 通路内外部均成立 |
| 1AVB / PR timing | Not supported | PR 敏感，但不特异 |
| AFIB / atrial window | Not supported | primary operator 下为负 |
| SBRAD / rate pathway | Evidence-limited | 内外部方向为正，但外部 CI 跨 0 |

这一段的作用是说明：ResNet 虽然分类性能很高，但不是所有疾病都能给出合理的 pathway-specific evidence。

---

### SE-ResNet  
### 加入 channel-wise attention 的 SE-ResNet

SE-ResNet 的分类性能和 ResNet 几乎一样，Macro-F1 差异很小，统计上不可区分。更重要的是，它在 pathway audit 上和 ResNet 大体方向一致：CRBBB 和 CLBBB 都是 Pathway-supported；1AVB 和 AFIB 都是 Not supported。fileciteturn7file1

这说明 QRS morphology pathway 的结论不是 ResNet 一个模型偶然得到的，而是在另一个 CNN 变体上也能复现。

但 SE-ResNet 也暴露了一个问题：早期 zero-masking 下 SE-ResNet 的 ASS 系统性更负，后来被解释为 operator-specific artifact。这再次支持论文的一个方法学观点：

> 模型架构会影响 pathway evidence，但扰动算子本身也会强烈影响 ASS，不能把算子当作无关实现细节。

---

### Lightweight 1D Transformer  
### 轻量级 1D Transformer

Transformer 的作用是展示 architecture heterogeneity。

它整体分类性能低于 ResNet，尤其在 SBRAD 和 AFIB 等 rhythm disorders 上明显弱；但 BBB 检测基本保持，CRBBB 和 CLBBB 的 F1 与 ResNet 接近。扰动审计进一步证明：Transformer 对 QRS→BBB 的 pathway 仍然支持，但对 1AVB、AFIB、SBRAD 都不支持。fileciteturn7file1

这个结果说明两点：

第一，**模型分类性能差一点，不代表它在所有通路上都没价值**。Transformer 虽然整体弱，但 QRS morphology pathway 仍然能通过审计。

第二，**perturbation sensitivity 不等于 pathway specificity**。Transformer 对很多扰动都更敏感，PSS 往往更大，但 control perturbation 也更大，所以 ASS 仍可能为负。

这其实是 Discussion 中一个很重要的提醒：  
不能看到某个模型被扰动影响很大，就直接说它用了正确通路。

---

### XGBoost variants  
### XGBoost 特征空间模型

XGBoost 在 Discussion 中不是 waveform matched-control tiering 的核心模型，而是 feature-space cross-check。

它说明不同模型类别可能使用不同信息通道。最典型的是 AFIB：XGBoost 的 AFIB 检测更依赖 AV-conduction timing features，而不是 rhythm features；但三个 raw-signal 模型在 RR irregularity 上接近 null，在 atrial-window 上 ASS 为负。fileciteturn7file4

这说明：

> 不同模型可能用重叠但不完全相同的信息。只审计一个模型，很容易把某个模型的解释误当成“这个任务”的解释。

这一节最后给出 methodological implication：扰动算子会显著影响 audit conclusion。单一 zero-masking 研究可能得出完全不同结论；因此 pathway claim 必须报告 operator sensitivity，而 linear interpolation 被推荐为 primary operator，因为它更能保持连续性、减少边界伪影。fileciteturn8file3

---

## B. Why Discrimination Metrics Alone Are Insufficient  
## 为什么单靠判别指标不够

这一节直接回应全文题目 **Beyond Discrimination**。

论文明确说：F1、AUROC、AUPRC 是必要的，但不足以判断模型是否用了 disease-consistent signal pathway。所有五个疾病在 ResNet 上 AUROC 都超过 0.98；如果只看 discrimination metrics，会觉得所有任务都做得很好。fileciteturn10file2

但 audit 结果完全不同：

| 类型 | 例子 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| Not supported | 1AVB、AFIB、部分 SBRAD | 模型预测好，但没有通路特异性证据 |
| Evidence-limited | SBRAD-ResNet | 有一定证据，但外部不确定性仍存在 |
| Pathway-supported | CRBBB、CLBBB | QRS morphology 通路稳定成立 |

所以 Discussion 的观点是：

> 高 AUROC 只能说明模型会分，但不能说明模型是“按医学机制在分”。

这一节还补充了反向情况：一个模型不一定要有最高 discrimination 才有有价值的 pathway behavior。Transformer 整体性能低于 ResNet，但在 BBB 上仍保留 QRS morphology pathway evidence。  
因此，audit 评估的是一个和 discrimination 不同的维度：**模型是否使用了疾病相关的特异性信号区域**。

---

## C. The Limits of Post-Hoc Explainability  
## 后验解释方法的局限

这一节是 Discussion 中最有攻击性的部分，主要批评传统 explainability workflow。

传统做法通常是：扰动某个目标区域，如果模型性能下降，就说模型依赖这个区域。论文认为这不够，因为它只证明了 **pathway sensitivity**，没有证明 **pathway specificity**。

1AVB 是最清楚的例子。PR-window occlusion 让 AUROC 下降 0.226，医学上也很合理，因为 PR interval 定义了 1AVB。传统 perturbation explainability 到这里就会停下，并声称模型依赖 PR-segment。fileciteturn7file1

但 matched QRS control 让这个结论反转：QRS perturbation 更强，导致 ASS 为负，而且这种反转在 CODE、PTB-XL、多个算子、多个架构中都成立。fileciteturn7file1

这一节的核心句可以概括为：

> 一个目标区域扰动效果很大，并不代表这个区域是最特异、最关键的；它可能只是模型整体依赖的一个相关区域。

然后论文进一步指出，除了 matched controls，还需要另外两个保护机制：

### 1. Operator selection  
CRBBB 是例子。zero-masking 下看起来外部 pathway specificity 失败，PTB-XL ASS 为负；但 primary linear interpolation 下，外部 ASS 明显为正。也就是说，算子选择可以把结论从“失败”变成“成功”。fileciteturn10file3

### 2. External transfer  
AFIB 是例子。zero-masking 下看似 cross-dataset positive，但 linear interpolation 下两个数据集都为负，因此原来的 positive 被解释为 operator artifact。fileciteturn8file3

这一节最终把方法学设计总结为三个必要部分：

> matched controls + operator selection + external transfer

三者分别防止三种假阳性：

| 设计 | 防止的问题 |
|---|---|
| matched controls | 防止 target-only perturbation 假阳性 |
| operator selection | 防止 zero-masking / 算子伪影 |
| external transfer | 防止只在内部数据成立的解释结论 |

---

## D. Relationship to Prior Work  
## 与已有工作的关系

这一节把本文放回 ECG explainability 文献中。

论文说，大多数已有 ECG 解释研究主要用 saliency maps 或 single-region perturbation 来证明某些区域会影响预测；也有一些工作开始构建更临床化的 ECG explanation framework。本文不是要替代这些解释方法，而是提出一个更严格的 **explanation evaluation method**。fileciteturn9file0

它和已有工作的区别主要有两个：

第一，本文要求 target-region perturbation 必须和 anatomically matched controls 比较。  
这比“目标区域扰动后性能下降”更严格，因为它能发现 1AVB 这种 false-positive pathway claim。

第二，本文要求在 frozen-weight transfer 到独立数据集后重新测试 pathway specificity。  
这解决的是解释结论是否只是某个数据集特有的问题。

所以这节的定位是：

> 本文不是生成新的解释图，而是审计已有模型解释是否真的支持 pathway-specific claim。

这句话很重要。它能避免审稿人误解：作者不是在提出新的 saliency 方法，而是在提出一套更严格的解释评估协议。

---

## E. Methodological Implications  
## 方法学启示

这一节把全文结果上升成可推广的方法学规则。

---

### The protocol is model-agnostic by design  
### 协议本身是模型无关的

论文强调，这套 protocol 可以用于任何接受 12-lead ECG input 的分类器。作者在 XGBoost、ResNet、SE-ResNet、Transformer 上都做了示范，说明它不依赖某一种模型结构。fileciteturn8file3

但这里的重点不是“我们测试了很多模型所以更强”，而是：

> 同一套 audit protocol 可以揭示不同模型使用信号通道的差异。

例如 Transformer 有 rhythm weakness，XGBoost 在 AFIB 上使用 complementary feature channel，这些都是单模型研究看不到的。

---

### Matched controls are not optional  
### matched controls 不是可选项

这一段再次回到 1AVB。大 target-pathway effect 可以和更大的 non-target dependence 共存。没有 matched controls，1AVB 会被误判为 timing-specific success。fileciteturn8file0

所以论文实际上在制定一个更严格的解释标准：

> 所有 pathway claim 都必须通过 matched-control specificity comparison。

ASS 就是把这个要求量化的指标。

---

### External transfer separates stable from unstable pathway claims  
### 外部迁移区分稳定和不稳定的通路结论

这一段强调 external transfer 的价值。

CRBBB 和 CLBBB 在三个架构上都通过 PTB-XL 外部验证，说明 QRS morphology pathway 是本文最稳定、最可信的 positive finding。1AVB 在外部数据中仍为负，说明 matched-control failure 可复现。AFIB 在外部数据中也显示 zero-masking positive 是 artifact。fileciteturn8file0

SBRAD 则展示了外部验证的另一种价值：ResNet 内部为正，外部方向也为正但 CI 跨 0，所以只能 Evidence-limited；SE-ResNet 内外部方向反转，所以不能支持。  
这说明 external transfer 不只是“加一个结果”，而是用来区分稳定证据和不稳定证据。

---

### Interpretation boundaries  
### 解释边界

这是 Discussion 中非常重要的一段，因为它主动收缩 claims，避免过度解释。

论文区分了四层证据：fileciteturn8file0

| 层级 | 含义 | 本文是否支持 |
|---|---|---|
| Pathway sensitivity | 扰动目标区域会造成性能下降 | 支持 |
| Pathway specificity | 目标区域影响超过 matched controls | 支持，这是 ASS 的核心 |
| Mechanistic validity | 模型使用了和医生一样的生理机制 | 不直接支持 |
| Clinical validity | 机制经过医生标注或临床结局验证 | 不支持，需要未来研究 |

这一节的态度很稳健：  
作者说 Pathway-supported 并不等于模型真的像医生一样推理，也不等于模型可以临床部署。它只表示：

> 在 primary operator 下，模型对疾病相关区域的扰动比对 control 区域的扰动更敏感。

这能有效防止审稿人质疑“你们是不是把 perturbation result 说成因果机制了”。

---

### Patient-level splitting, multi-seed training, and comprehensive metrics  
### 患者级划分、多随机种子和完整指标

这一段是对实验规范的总结。  
论文认为，patient-level splitting 防止数据泄漏；multi-seed training 验证训练稳定性；完整指标避免只看单一性能。表示学习层面的 representation ladder 也说明 rhythm、morphology、timing 三类信息互补，显式 proxy features 有时也能恢复临床相关信号，而不一定全部依赖 end-to-end learning。fileciteturn8file0

---

## F. Limitations  
## 局限性

这一节列了 12 条，比较完整。可以按逻辑分成五类来看。

---

### 1) Single external validation dataset  
### 只有一个外部验证数据集

外部验证只用了 PTB-XL。虽然 PTB-XL fold 10 是 cardiologist-validated，增强了可信度，但它仍然只是一个德国人群、特定设备和采集流程的数据集。论文承认，还需要更多国家、设备、人群的数据集验证泛化性。fileciteturn8file0

另外，threshold retuning 用的是 PTB-XL fold 9，而 fold 9 不是完全 cardiologist-adjudicated，这会引入额外 label noise。

---

### 2) Automated labels, not physician-confirmed  
### CODE-15% 标签来自自动解释系统，不是医生确认

这是非常关键的局限。CODE-15% 的标签来自自动 ECG interpretation，而不是 cardiologist adjudication。  
这可能导致模型学习自动标注系统的逻辑，而不是医生诊断机制。PTB-XL fold 10 提供了一个外部可信度缓冲，但不能完全消除 CODE 内部分析的 label circularity 风险。fileciteturn8file0

论文还提到 PR>200ms rule baseline 的 AUROC 为 0.783，而 ResNet 外部 AUROC 为 0.937，说明 frozen transfer 不是简单 PR threshold 能解释的；但这仍然不能替代医生确认的 CODE 子集。

---

### 3) Clinical-MVP features are pragmatic proxies, not comprehensive measurements  
### Clinical-MVP 特征只是实用代理，不是完整临床测量

Clinical-MVP 特征包括 PR proxy，但缺少 T-wave morphology、QT interval、ST-segment measurements、详细 P/QRS/T onset/offset 等。  
因此这些 feature gains 可能混合了真实生理信息、delineation heuristic、信号质量、以及与自动标签的对齐。fileciteturn8file0

换句话说，Clinical-MVP 不是临床 gold standard，只是一个有用的 proxy feature set。

---

### 4) Perturbation operator sensitivity is an important concern  
### 扰动算子敏感性是重要问题

论文承认，即使采用 linear interpolation 作为 primary operator，也不能说这个算子就是唯一最佳方案。operator-comparison battery 显示：

- zero-masking 会产生 hard-boundary artifacts；
- beat-conditioned inpainting 太保守，区分力不足；
- linear interpolation 目前最可解释、最稳定。

但更大的领域问题是：perturbation literature 还没有统一标准。任何 single-operator perturbation study 的 pathway claim 都应该被视为 provisional，直到经过 operator variation 验证。fileciteturn8file0

---

### 5) External PTB-XL perturbation experiments are now complete for all five diseases  
### 外部 PTB-XL 扰动实验已经覆盖五个疾病，但仍有细节问题

这一条其实更像是说明当前版本已经补齐外部审计：15 个 architecture-disease pairs 都完成了 primary-operator PTB-XL audit。  
但 SBRAD 仍然有不确定性：ResNet external ASS 方向为正，但 CI 跨 0；SE-ResNet 出现 internal negative、external positive 的 sign reversal；Transformer 在两个数据集上都为负。fileciteturn8file0

这一条说明 SBRAD 仍然是最需要进一步研究的疾病通路。

---

### 6) No subgroup or fairness analysis  
### 没有亚组和公平性分析

论文没有按年龄、性别、站点、设备、记录质量等分组分析，因此不能推出 fairness claim。

---

### 7) Patient-level splitting without patient-level aggregation analysis  
### 做了患者级划分，但没有研究患者级聚合

研究防止了同一患者跨 train/test 泄漏，但没有分析当一个患者有多条 ECG 时，如何进行 patient-level aggregation。

---

### 8) Statistical inference with patient-level clustering  
### 统计推断中的患者聚类问题

Results 中的 permutation tests 和 DeLong comparisons 是 sample-level inference，样本约 69,500 条 ECG，来自约 47,000 个患者。  
但同一患者多条 ECG 之间可能相关，因此有效自由度更接近患者数，而不是 ECG 数。论文建议读者更重视 patient-level bootstrap CIs，而不是 sample-level p-values。fileciteturn8file0

---

### 9) Metadata and acquisition confounding remain possible  
### 元数据和采集流程混杂仍可能存在

不同设备、采集流程、数据集特征可能影响内部性能和外部迁移差异。论文没有完全排除这些 confounding。

---

### 10) Limited to 5 cardiac conditions  
### 只研究了 5 个心电诊断

目前只覆盖 1AVB、CRBBB、CLBBB、SBRAD、AFIB，不能代表所有 ECG 疾病。

---

### 11) No cardiologist review  
### 没有医生人工审查失败案例

如果有 cardiologist review failure cases，会更强地支持临床解释。

---

### 12) Hybrid models unexplored  
### 没有探索混合模型

论文没有研究把 Clinical-MVP features 和 learned representations 结合起来的 hybrid model。这可能进一步提高性能和解释性。

---

## G. Future Work  
## 未来工作

这一节基本是对 Limitations 的正向展开。

未来工作包括：

第一，继续扩展 cross-architecture perturbation audit，尤其验证 architecture-dependent ASS patterns 是否能在更多外部数据集上保持。

第二，使用更多独立数据集，覆盖不同国家、设备、人群，增强泛化性。

第三，构建 cardiologist-adjudicated CODE-15% 子集，用于正式量化 label noise。

第四，做 lead-stratified perturbation experiments，并结合医生审查失败案例，让 anatomical granularity 更强。

第五，把 audit panel 扩展到更多 ECG diagnoses，并加入 subgroup/fairness analysis。

第六，探索 hybrid models，把 handcrafted clinical features 和 learned representations 结合起来。

第七，设计更真实的 perturbation，比如 physiologically motivated simulations，而不是简单 signal removal。

第八，推动 perturbation operator 的社区标准，包括 operator selection、preregistration 和 minimal reporting requirements。fileciteturn7file0

这一节的核心是：

> 当前工作证明了 matched-control audit 的价值，但真正走向机制解释和临床可信，还需要更多数据集、医生审查、更真实的扰动、更系统的算子标准。

---

# 整个 Discussion 的故事线

Discussion 可以压缩成这一条主线：

> Results 证明了高 AUROC 并不等于模型用了正确医学通路；Discussion 则进一步说明，可靠的 pathway claim 至少需要 matched controls、operator sensitivity analysis 和 external transfer 三个条件。同时，本文的 Pathway-supported 只是 pathway specificity 证据，不等于机制因果证明，也不等于临床可部署。

更直白地说，这一章是在帮论文“守边界”和“立标准”：

一方面，它立标准：  
**解释研究不能只说某区域扰动后性能下降，还要证明它强于 matched controls，并且不是算子伪影，也不是只在内部数据成立。**

另一方面，它守边界：  
**本文不是证明模型像医生一样推理，也不是证明临床可用，而是证明在一个受控扰动协议下，某些模型-疾病对具有 pathway-specific evidence。**
